method: One agent read the published primary-paper PDFs and manually annotated selected experiment passages at paragraph level. Annotations describe ordering, evidence placement, and claim boundaries; they do not score scientific correctness. Source files were processed outside the repository with pdftotext. Only independent structural summaries, locators, and PDF checksums are retained, not extracted prose. This is a purposive calibration sample, not an independent multi-reviewer study or a frequency estimate.
scope: Seven existing corpus sources, twelve passages, covering reinforcement learning, world models, embodied AI, and VLA. This supplements the 80-paper document-level detector study without adding papers to the coverage count.

annotations.locator: Section 4.1, Comparison to existing methods, printed pp. 6-7; Figures 4-6 and Appendix G
annotations.observation: The paragraph moves from overall performance to difficult task families and training instability, while directing detailed task results and gradients to separate displays.
annotations.numeric_role: Task count establishes evaluation scope; individual curve values are not recited.
annotations.transfer_rule: Use an aggregate finding to motivate an existing diagnostic or difficult-regime comparison.
annotations.boundary: Do not infer matched resources from this narrative: baseline parameter counts and update ratios differ and are disclosed in setup.

annotations.locator: Section 4.1, Scaling TD-MPC2 to 317M parameters, printed p. 7; Figure 7 and Table 1
annotations.observation: The paragraph describes growth with model size and separates that observation from a formal scaling law. Costs and per-model scores remain in Table 1.
annotations.numeric_role: Model scale identifies the tested range, rather than repeating the score at each scale.
annotations.transfer_rule: State a supported trend across a range; retain the resource cost and distinguish observation from extrapolation.
annotations.boundary: Do not adopt the paper's expectation of further improvement as a general rule or claim saturation was statistically tested.

annotations.observation: A table contains per-game scores; the concluding prose qualifies competitiveness by how many games satisfy the comparison rather than listing scores.
annotations.numeric_role: The count of covered games constrains the breadth of the claim.
annotations.transfer_rule: Use coverage and exceptions to qualify a cross-task conclusion; keep baseline provenance recoverable.
annotations.boundary: The sampled paper calls dispersion variance in the caption and standard deviation in the prose. Do not transfer that ambiguity into a template.

annotations.observation: The passage asks about sparse rewards, describes the delayed-reward setting, and contrasts methods' responses without enumerating the table cells.
annotations.numeric_role: Full dense and delayed scores remain in Table 6; the prose explains the experimental contrast.
annotations.transfer_rule: Explain what a controlled setting changes before drawing the corresponding empirical conclusion.
annotations.boundary: Do not generalize from delayed rewards on these datasets to every sparse-reward problem.

annotations.locator: Section 5.2, Model Scaling and Data Scaling, printed pp. 6-7; Figure 4
annotations.observation: Model-size and data-size comparisons receive distinct paragraphs. Selective data-budget anchors support efficiency claims; a representation-based explanation is labeled as a hypothesis.
annotations.numeric_role: Capacity range and selected data fractions identify the tested axes rather than repeating every success rate.
annotations.transfer_rule: Separate scale from data efficiency and distinguish an explanatory hypothesis from the measured trend.
annotations.boundary: Do not copy a hypothesis into a new paper when that paper has no corresponding evidence.

annotations.locator: Section 5.2, Progressive Generalization, printed p. 7; Figure 5
annotations.observation: The paragraph compares degradation across increasingly difficult levels and acknowledges that all methods deteriorate on novel tasks.
annotations.numeric_role: Selected degradation contrasts describe the relative advantage while preserving a common failure boundary.
annotations.transfer_rule: Place the difficult-regime exception beside a favorable generalization claim.
annotations.boundary: Lower degradation is not an absence of degradation or demonstrated real-robot transfer.

annotations.locator: Section V, The tradeoff in action horizon, printed p. 5; Figure 6
annotations.observation: The passage relates action consistency to slower feedback and reports a tested horizon choice, rather than claiming longer horizons always help.
annotations.numeric_role: The selected horizon illustrates the tested operating choice; the full sweep stays in the figure.
annotations.transfer_rule: Describe both sides of a design trade-off and keep the chosen setting conditional on tested tasks.
annotations.boundary: A selected horizon is not a universal optimum or proof of a mechanism.

annotations.locator: Section VI.A, Result Analysis, printed p. 6; Table V and Figure 8
annotations.observation: The analysis uses selected success and overlap comparisons, then examines stage-transition behavior and observed baseline failures. It does not recite all encoder variants.
annotations.numeric_role: Main outcome anchors and failure counts serve different evidential functions.
annotations.transfer_rule: Use actually observed behavior to extend an outcome comparison; quantitative and qualitative evidence need distinct roles.
annotations.boundary: Some causal explanations in the paper are stronger than a generic template should allow; retain the new task's actual control limits.

annotations.locator: Section 4.1, printed p. 5; Figure 2 and Table 1
annotations.observation: The favorable outcome is followed by a seed-level instability on Finger Spin, with selected return anchors explaining why aggregate dispersion matters.
annotations.numeric_role: Seed outcomes diagnose an exception instead of merely adding more favorable averages.
annotations.transfer_rule: Explain consequential variability as part of the result, not as a footnote detached from the claim.
annotations.boundary: Do not equate low variance with high quality or use a few seeds as proof of stability.

annotations.observation: The diagnostic describes reconstructions and nearest-neighbor behavior, then acknowledges that backgrounds can still influence the representation.
annotations.numeric_role: Training steps identify the visualization condition, not a new performance ranking.
annotations.transfer_rule: A diagnostic can refine a mechanism hypothesis while revealing what the method has not solved.
annotations.boundary: A visualization does not uniquely identify a causal explanation; retain alternatives.

annotations.locator: Section 5.1, clean depth sensor finding, printed p. 15696; Table 2
annotations.observation: The passage contrasts sensor modalities, selects a severe-corruption gap, and notes the cost of adding sensors instead of ranking every corruption row.
annotations.numeric_role: A range of gaps anchors the named severe conditions.
annotations.transfer_rule: Name the sensing assumption and cost when interpreting robustness, not just the favorable metric.
annotations.boundary: The clean depth sensor is an explicit assumption; this does not show robustness when all modalities are corrupted.

annotations.observation: Real-robot performance is organized by task families and capabilities rather than by model rows; the trial denominator is established before the analysis.
annotations.numeric_role: Attempts define the evaluation denominator while per-task success rates stay in the display.
annotations.transfer_rule: Separate generalization axes and group comparisons by the tested capability, with shared protocol reported once.
annotations.boundary: Borrow the organization, not broad causal claims about semantic or spatial understanding from success rates alone.

limitations: Selected passages do not establish that any one opening, sentence count, numeric density, or transition is standard across venues.
No blind writer or human expert evaluated this synthesis; improved professional prose is an unverified effectiveness hypothesis.
Accepted papers may contain ambiguous statistics or overstated interpretations. The library adopts structural strategies, not every source claim or adjective.
PDF checksums identify the reviewed bytes, not publication quality or permanent future availability.
